description: The RFL Championship / League 1 completeness sweep Package 06 never ran. Its purpose is to prove the omitted estate hides no additional material high-value venues — finding none is a successful result.

source_families.family: 2026 RFL Championship (merged former Championship + League One tier)

evidence.note: Official RFL club list for the current Championship -- 20 active clubs (21 originally admitted, minus Featherstone Rovers, excluded 9 Jan 2026)
Full club+ground table for all 20 active clubs plus the Featherstone/Salford/Halifax exclusion and readmission history
Secondary corroboration of club/ground pairings (noisier extraction, used only to cross-check current sponsor names, not as primary source)
RFL's own article confirming Championship and League One were merged into one division for 2026

source_families.notes: For 2026 the RFL merged the Championship and League One into a single 20-club division -- there is no longer a separate RFL League 1 competition to walk (see the dedicated 'RFL League 1 (2026)' entry below). All 20 clubs' home grounds were established and diffed against EXISTING-ESTATE.txt: every one is already held. 14 are already RUGBY_LEAGUE_GROUND/STADIUM entries; 6 are legitimate groundshares already held under a different class -- Doncaster (Club Doncaster Sports Village, FOOTBALL_GROUND), Halifax (The Shay, FOOTBALL_GROUND), London Broncos (Plough Lane, FOOTBALL_GROUND), Oldham (Boundary Park, FOOTBALL_GROUND) and Salford (CorpAcq Stadium -- current sponsor name for the ground previously called AJ Bell Stadium / Salford Community Stadium -- held as RUGBY_UNION_GROUND). Zero new venues found. Featherstone Rovers, the 21st admitted club, was excluded before the season started; its ground is covered in row-dispositions.jsonl, not here.

evidence.note: RFL's own confirmation that 'the Betfred Championship and League One competitions will be combined in a single division outside the Betfred Super League in 2026'
Corroborates League One no longer exists as an independent competition from 2026

source_families.notes: This is a structural finding, not a skipped sweep: RFL League 1 was merged into the Championship for the 2026 season, so it has no independent 2026 club estate of its own to walk. Its former member clubs are the same clubs already walked under the '2026 RFL Championship' entry above. Recorded as its own row so the builder does not read 'League 1 not walked' as a gap.

source_families.family: UK Athletics / British Athletics National Championships venue rotation

evidence.note: Fetched: confirms Alexander Stadium, Birmingham as 2025 outdoor host (2-3 Aug 2025), returning after 2019.
Fetched: confirms Manchester Regional Arena as 2024 host (29-30 June 2024); decathlon/heptathlon at Alexander Stadium, 10,000m at Parliament Hill, London.

source_families.notes: The three rotating national outdoor/indoor championship venues identified — Alexander Stadium, Manchester Regional Arena, and Utilita Arena Birmingham (2025 British Indoor Championships) — are all already held in EXISTING-ESTATE.txt as CONFIRMED_1000_PLUS. The britishathletics.org.uk primary announcement article surfaced by search ('venues-confirmed-for-national-championships-in-2024-and-2025') returned HTTP 404 on fetch; Wikipedia championship-year pages were fetched as corroborating sources instead. Parliament Hill, London (used for one event, the 10,000m) is a small local track with no permanent stand and was excluded as immaterial. No venue outside the existing estate was surfaced by this family.

evidence.note: Search result / listing confirms 2026 National Senior and U18 Championships (29-30 Aug 2026) at Aberdeen Sports Village.
Fetched: official venue page, outdoor Chris Anderson Stadium stand seats 500 spectators.
Confirms Scotstoun Stadium, Glasgow, has just had a new 400m athletics track laid as host of Athletics/Para Athletics at the 2026 Commonwealth Games.

source_families.notes: Scotland's national championships rotate across Grangemouth Stadium (already held, CAPACITY_UNVERIFIED_HIGH_VALUE_CANDIDATE), Scotstoun Stadium, Glasgow (already held under RUGBY_UNION_GROUND — now also nationally material for athletics as the 2026 Commonwealth Games track venue), and, newly for 2026, Aberdeen Sports Village for the Senior/U18 championships. Aberdeen Sports Village is not in EXISTING-ESTATE.txt; fetched directly and confirmed below threshold (500-seat stand). No other Scottish venue outside the existing estate was surfaced as plausibly reaching 1,000.
